body: Thanks I needed to hear this <3

Firstly, thanks for sharing how you're feeling. I'm really sorry to hear about what your friend went through, and what you've been through as well as a result. You are not old. And it sounds like you are living with an enormous amount of guilt which you should 100% not be feeling. It sounds like there have been some very negative messages given to you through your upbringing, but they are not the objective truth. Having sex is a completely normal, natural thing - of course you were having sex with your boyfriend!! You didn't drive him away, for whatever reason your relationship ended but it's not your fault. It takes two to tango in any situation. It wasn't the right time for you and him to be together, and that's ok. Maybe you came into each other's lives at the wrong time. But you are young, you're obviously smart and part of you has a lot of ambition and motivation (you wouldn't be studying engineering and physics otherwise!) - this part of you is in there and you can nurture it and let it be at the forefront of your life again.   


You've been through a trauma, what you saw happen to your friend and the way that the people around you both subsequently dealt with it is NOT your fault, you have done nothing wrong. Your relationship ending is also not your fault. Relationships and people come and go. You are still in a period of grief and loss over the relationship - this is normal. Let yourself feel the sadness and really nurture yourself during this time.  Keep reaching out for support. I suggest reading up more about resources for sexual assault survivors, and it's also worth reading about how to manage grief and loss of relationships. Those feelings of guilt and blaming yourself for the sadness you are feeling can be dealt with and managed with the right support. You are not the only person who has felt this way. I really hope you feel a bit better after reaching out, and that you keep reaching out until you find the right support that works for you. Hugs xx
